svg.aria-label: Bar chart of reported image-level AUROC on the AeBAD-S aero-engine blade anomaly benchmark, where the test images shift in illumination, viewpoint and background compared with training. Reverse Distillation reports about 81.0, the original MMR method about 84.7, MSFRN about 87.1 according to a leaderboard, and NFAD, a 2026 preprint that filters nuisance directions in feature space, 91.0 on average. NFAD's weakest split is the view shift at 86.0. The message: illumination and background shift are being solved; viewpoint shift is the remaining gap. Numbers come from different papers and a third-party leaderboard and are not a controlled comparison.
svg.title: Blade anomaly detection under acquisition shift (AeBAD-S)
svg.text: Blade anomaly detection under acquisition shift (AeBAD-S, image AUROC)
Author- or leaderboard-reported numbers from different papers; read as a trend, not a controlled comparison.
Illumination and background shift respond to feature-space nuisance filtering; viewpoint (geometry) does not —
which is why borescope pipelines add templated imaging, turning-tool indexing and per-blade registration.
